what_this_is: The task-level test of the static-YaRN penalty: a full Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass served at 1,000,000 tokens via Qwen's official static YaRN, against the otherwise-comparable 262k-native arm. Intended to corroborate the token-level result in docs/46 s31. It corroborates the DIRECTION but does NOT independently establish the effect.

statistics.VERDICT: NOT statistically significant at either cut. The direction matches the token-level result and the magnitude is plausible, but with 18 discordant pairs a 13-5 split is p = 0.096, so this arm CORROBORATES s31 and does not independently prove anything. The recommendation rests on s31's token-level measurement, whose 95 % CI [8.42e-03, 1.29e-02] excludes zero by a wide margin against a bit-identical control.

why_the_split_by_failure_mode_matters.reading: Because the total timeout count is identical, the clock budget did not change between arms; the timeouts merely landed on different tasks. The asymmetry lives in the NON-timeout failures, which is where a fidelity effect would show up rather than a scheduling one. That is the most YaRN-consistent feature of the data, and it is still only p = 0.11.

confounds_stated: CONCURRENCY DIFFERS: C16 here versus C32 in the reference arm. The direction of that confound FAVOURS this arm - less contention, so fewer contention-induced timeouts - which is why a -8 result is not explained by it and if anything is understated.
WALL CLOCK IS NOT COMPARABLE: 3.60 h against 2.35 h is 1.53x at HALF the concurrency, so it is a function of the shard width, not of the rope. No wall-clock claim is made.

Both arms are SINGLE pass, so both carry best-of-1 variance; the 262k arm alone showed 5 regressions against its own best-of-2 reference. Churn of this size is expected and is why the sign test, not the net, is quoted.
The 2 RuntimeErrors in both arms are the same two nested-virt qemu voids, unattemptable on this host.
conclusion: Serving at 1M via static YaRN scored 48/89 against 262k-native's 56/89. Read together with s31 - where the same rope change moved the next-token distribution by 1.057e-02 with the window itself proven fidelity-free - the task-level and token-level results point the same way. The task-level arm is the weaker of the two pieces of evidence and should be cited as corroboration, never as the primary result.
